finding.claim: reset_password_loose compares the stored reset token with loose == against an untyped $token, so a boolean true (or a magic-hash collision) passes the check and the password is replaced without the real token.
finding.source: $token parameter (reset.php:2), attacker-controlled if the caller passes decoded JSON or other typed input unchanged
finding.sink: UPDATE users SET pw at reset.php:5-6

trace.note: stored token fetched for $email; a row exists only if a reset was requested for that address
$row['token'] == $token; any non-empty, non-'0' string == true evaluates true
password overwritten for the victim's email

finding.guards_checked: No === comparison, no is_string/type check, no hash_equals in this function. Reachability depends on the caller, which is not in the repo. The safer comparison exists in reset_password at reset.php:14.

verdict.guard_found: None inside reset_password_loose. The only check is `$row &&` at reset.php:4, which just requires a reset row for the email; an attacker can trigger that by requesting a reset for the victim's address. reset_password (reset.php:14, hash_equals with (string)$token) is a separate function and is not used by reset_password_loose.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: reset.php:2 takes $token untyped, reset.php:4 uses loose `==` against the stored token, and reset.php:5-6 overwrites the password, so a boolean `true` would pass on PHP 8. Whether that is reachable cannot be decided because the repo contains only this file and no caller; if the caller passes form or query input, PHP gives strings, and a magic-hash collision needs a numeric-looking stored token, so reachability hinges on code outside the repo.

finding.claim: reset_password never deletes or expires the reset token after use, so a leaked token can be replayed indefinitely, including after the user has changed their password.
finding.source: A previously obtained reset token (leaked email, log, referrer)
finding.sink: UPDATE users SET pw at reset.php:15-16

trace.note: token row selected by email with no timestamp condition
returns true with no DELETE from resets and no consumption step

finding.guards_checked: hash_equals is correct and timing-safe. No one-time-use enforcement and no expiry in this file. Expiry may exist in a cron job or the schema, which are not in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none in the repo. hash_equals at reset.php:14 is a timing-safe comparison, not a use-once or expiry check. No DELETE or UPDATE on resets anywhere in reset.php (only one file exists in the directory). The only other query-side control is the email lookup at reset.php:13, which does not check a timestamp.
verdict.reason: reset_password at reset.php:12-20 updates the password on a token match (lines 14-16) and returns true at line 17 without deleting or invalidating the resets row, so a leaked token keeps matching after use; the only unverified part is whether a schema constraint or out-of-repo cron prunes the resets table, which would limit the "indefinitely" wording but not the replay itself.

finding.claim: If resets.token is NULL or empty, hash_equals receives an empty string and an empty submitted token matches, allowing a reset with no token.
finding.source: $token set to null or '' by the attacker
finding.sink: UPDATE users SET pw at reset.php:15-16

trace.note: row fetched; token column may be NULL or ''

finding.guards_checked: (string) cast present but does not reject empty input. Reachability depends on the resets schema, which is not in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none effective. reset.php:13 fetches the row with no filter on token, and reset.php:14 casts the submitted token with (string) but never rejects an empty value. The `if ($row && ...)` at reset.php:14 only guards against a missing row, not an empty token. Only reset.php exists in the repo, so no code creates or constrains the resets rows.
verdict.reason: The trace lines match the code: reset.php:14 calls hash_equals($row['token'], (string)$token), and reset.php:15-16 updates the password. Whether an attacker can reach the match depends on whether any resets row for a real email has a NULL or empty token, and the schema that governs this is not in the repo, so reachability cannot be decided from the code available.
